tests.experiment: Independent replication at T 0.6 of the stratified post-minus-pre paired gap (RL plain minus base cue) on the clean harder 328, matched on RL answer length, using different samples and a different decoding setting from tests.json.
tests.recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_hard.jsonl (base, cue, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s2800-01/out/P_hard.jsonl (RL step 2,800, plain, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95). If a file has more than one row per unique_id, keep the row with the smallest sample value. Keep only unique_ids whose flag == 'none' in results/rln3/rln3_overlap.json, join the two files on unique_id, and drop any unique_id missing from either file. Source label from rln3_overlap.json: post = AIME 2025 or HMMT Feb 2025; pre = every other source. right = (score == 1), using the stored v1 score field; cap hits and rows with no extracted answer count as their stored score (0 if score is null). Strata: sort the joined problems by the RL row's n_generated ascending, break ties by unique_id ascending, and cut into 4 consecutive groups of equal size (the remainder goes to the last group). In each stratum s and group g (post/pre), d_gs = mean over problems of (RL right - base right). w_s = (number of post problems in s) / (number of post problems). Drop any stratum that has post problems but no pre problems, and renormalise w over the remaining strata. G_g = sum_s w_s * d_gs. Statistic = 100 * (G_post - G_pre), in points.
tests.note: Files: s3 r3/base-01/out/F_hard.jsonl (cached at runs/theory-tests/duel-r4-m08/base01_F_hard.jsonl) and r3/s2800-01/out/P_hard.jsonl (cached as s2800_P_hard.jsonl); overlap file is studies/rlneurons/results/rln3/rln3_overlap.json (the recipe's results/rln3/... path is relative to the rlneurons study; no file exists at the repo-root path). Overlap flags under sets.hard.flags are keyed by problem_index, not unique_id, so the 328 filter and the post/pre source label are looked up through each row's problem_index (checked while reading the format: every row's unique_id prefix matches the overlap source). Both files have exactly one row per unique_id (sample 0), so the smallest-sample rule changes nothing. right = score == 1, and a null score counts as 0. Strata are cut on the RL row's n_generated, ties broken by unique_id, 4 groups of floor(n/4) with the remainder in the last group. A stratum with pre problems but no post problems gets w=0, so it adds nothing to either G. A stratum with post problems but no pre problems is dropped and w is renormalised. Only 60 post problems (AIME 2025 + HMMT Feb 2025), so each stratum holds few post items and the number is noisy. alt_measured is a different statistic, not another reading: the unstratified gap 100*(mean d_post - mean d_pre) with no length matching. The recipe left no real ambiguity to read two ways.

tests.experiment: Independent replication at T 0.6 of the both-right base/RL length comparison: median log length ratio, pre-cutoff minus post-cutoff, on the clean harder 328.
tests.recipe: Same two files, row choice, 328 filter, join, drops and post/pre labels as the first test here (r3/base-01 F_hard.jsonl base cue; r3/s2800-01 P_hard.jsonl RL plain). Keep problems where score == 1 (stored v1) in both rows and cap_hit is false in both rows. For each kept problem, r = ln(base n_generated / RL n_generated). Statistic = median of r over kept pre problems minus median of r over kept post problems (for an even count, the median is the mean of the two middle values). If no post problem is kept, recompute with the cap_hit condition removed, keeping score == 1 in both rows.
tests.unit: difference of median log length ratios
tests.note: Same files, 328 filter (via problem_index), join and post/pre labels as k=1. Kept: score == 1 in both rows and cap_hit is False in both. r = ln(base n_generated / RL n_generated). Statistic = median(pre r) - median(post r), even counts averaged. If no post problem survives, the script recomputes without the cap_hit condition (stderr reports whether that happened). If a group is still empty the script prints not_computable, because the recipe does not say what to do then. alt_measured uses n_new instead of n_generated (n_generated = n_new + 1 in the rows seen), so it should differ only slightly. The post group is small (at most 60 problems, fewer both-right), so the post median is noisy.

tests.experiment: MATH-500: per-token entropy of the RL model's own short right answers relative to its own long right answers (the RL-side counterpart of test 3).
tests.recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/rln5/map-01/checks.json (key per_row, list T2) and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. For each T2 row, per-token entropy e = sum_entropy_own / n_own. Drop rows with n_own == 0 or missing. Join with per_problem.json on problem_index. Keep problems with t2_right true and t2_cap_hit false. short = t2_generated_tokens <= 2000; long = t2_generated_tokens > 2000. Statistic = median e over short / median e over long (for an even count, the median is the mean of the two middle values).
tests.note: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/rln5/map-01/checks.json per_row.T2 and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json, both committed. e = sum_entropy_own / n_own. Rows with n_own missing or 0, or sum_entropy_own missing, are dropped. Join on problem_index. Kept: t2_right true (stored as int 1, so 1 is treated as true) and t2_cap_hit False. Split on per_problem t2_generated_tokens (<= 2000 short, > 2000 long). Ratio = median short / median long. alt_measured normalises by n_gen instead of n_own (n_own = n_gen + 1 in the rows seen), so it is only a tiny variant. Note: these are T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 generations, and the entropies come from teacher-forcing the stored answers under the RL model (own), as the checks.json fields name them.
